title: Rollup card unification and graceful fallback patterns for Console MVP
creator: Sofia Ramirez
description: Context: to hit the Console MVP date with acceptable engineering effort we need to reduce surface area for dashboard cards, tracing sampling, and cost breakdown detail. This ticket captures scope decisions that unify similar 'insight' cards into a single rollup card, replace full trace capture with a sampled lightweight tracer and span-count summary, and provide a progressive fallback UX when detailed telemetry is unavailable. Goal: deliver a cohesive minimal surface that surfaces actionable signals (errors, spikes, cost anomalies) while keeping engineering and data costs predictable.
scope_changes: Unify three existing card types (route-level latency, route-level throughput, and p50/p95 trend) into a single 'Route Rollup' card that shows compact sparkline + p50/p95 and a one-line anomaly badge.
Remove per-route deep cost breakdown in MVP; show only aggregated cost by model family and top-5 routes in the rollup card. Detailed per-token cost drilldown deferred to post-MVP.
Tracing: replace full trace view with 'sampled traces' for error-causing requests and a trace-count heatmap. Full waterfall trace view postponed to a later phase.

Fallback behavior: if tracing is not available or quota exceeded, rollup cards display a clear 'sampling' badge and a concise explanation with a CTA to enable Dedicated/Private tracing or increase quota.
Telemetry retention: reduce default retention for trace samples to 7 days for MVP to control storage costs; extended retention will be an opt-in paid feature.
Design: deliver compact card visual only; interactive drilldown beyond the rollup card limited to a single modal listing top anomalies + one sampled trace sample.
API surface: expose a single consolidated tenant-level metrics endpoint used by the rollup card rather than multiple specialized endpoints.
acceptance_criteria: Rollup card implemented and visible on Console home with unified data model for route metrics (sparkline, p50, p95, anomaly badge).
Backend endpoint returns consolidated payload within 120ms p95 under synthetic load (1k req/s test harness).
Cost view shows aggregated cost by model family and top-5 routes, with numbers matching billing within 3% for sampled window used in MVP.
Tracing UI surfaces a sampled-trace modal triggered for error-level events; at least one sampled trace rendered for each error type in a synthetic error injection test.
When tracing quota is exceeded or disabled, rollup cards display a non-blocking fallback state (sampling badge + link to quota/upgrade) and no error thrown to the page console.
E2E tests cover: rollup card render, fallback state, sampled trace modal open/close, and cost aggregation accuracy. Tests added to CI and passing.
Performance: aggregated dashboard page load (rollup cards only) p95 < 600ms in staging with 10 tenants simulated.
Design sign-off: UX review completed, and accessibility checklist items for the rollup card passed (contrast, keyboard nav, screen-reader labels).
Feature flag gating: new rollup card behind 'rollup-cards-v1' flag; default ON for MVP orgs in pilot cohort only.
decisions: Cut detailed per-route token-level cost drilldown to post-MVP to reduce billing integration work and frontend complexity.
Adopt sampled traces for MVP (error-first sampling) instead of full tracing to control storage and pipeline costs.
Consolidate metric endpoints to a single payload to simplify frontend logic and reduce network round-trips.
Retention set to 7 days for trace samples to keep early storage costs reasonable; customers requiring longer retention will be offered an opt-in plan.
Graceful fallback strategy chosen over blocking errors to prioritize console availability for all customers.
